answer: Rotation-gated cipher challenge. The registry assigns each identity a clock offset and requires a valid cipher response within one narrow slot per rotation cycle; responses outside the slot are dropped before verification. An attacker farming identities must keep every fake agent synchronized and awake through every cycle, paying continuous compute and monitoring cost per identity, which makes large sybil fleets economically idle. Honest agents need only a cheap local knoll timer, while the attacker's per-identity upkeep scales linearly, eroding any oasis of cheap bulk registration.
